C001130.narrative: Crockett votes most often on procedural matters in Congress, economics, and national security. In economics and public finance, she votes against most bills, including appropriations measures for military construction and agriculture. On armed forces and national security, she leans against more bills than she supports, and voted in favor of resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran. She votes in favor of most energy-related bills. Her votes on international affairs are split, with slightly more in favor than against.

H001095.narrative: Hunt votes most on Congress, economics, defense, energy, and international affairs issues. On defense and international affairs, he votes in favor most of the time — for example, he voted yes on the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act. On economics, he also leans in favor, including votes for bills like the Keeping Deposits Local Act and the American Access to Banking Act. On energy and Congress-related procedural votes, he leans against — voting no on bills like the Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative Reauthorization Act.

C001131.narrative: Casar votes most often on congressional procedures, economic issues, and defense and national security matters. On energy bills, he votes in favor far more than against. On spending and economic bills, he votes against more than in favor. He also votes against defense and international affairs bills more than in favor. For example, he voted yes on removing U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran under the War Powers Resolution, and voted no on military construction appropriations.

D000594.narrative: De La Cruz votes most often on congressional operations, energy policy, economics, military affairs, and international relations. She votes against most congressional procedure measures and energy efficiency programs, including bills to fund energy rebates and appliance efficiency rules. She votes in favor of most economic, military, and international affairs measures, including housing program expansions, defense funding, and requirements to exclude China from financial groups if China threatens Taiwan. Her voting pattern shows opposition to energy efficiency initiatives while supporting military and economic policies.

G000581.narrative: Gonzalez votes most often on congressional procedure, armed forces, and economic issues. On armed forces and national security bills, he votes in favor more often than against — he voted yes on removing U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran and yes on veterans' benefits expansion. On economics and public finance bills, he votes against proposals more often than in favor, including a no vote on military construction and Veterans Affairs appropriations. He votes in favor of international affairs and government operations proposals more often than against.

G000553.narrative: Rep. Al Green votes most often on congressional procedure, armed forces and national security, and economics and public finance. On economics and public finance, he votes against bills more often than in favor — including a vote against the military construction and Veterans Affairs appropriations bill. On armed forces and national security, his votes are split evenly between in favor and against; he voted in favor of directing the President to remove U.S. armed forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran. On government operations and politics, he votes in favor more often than against.

V000134.narrative: Van Duyne votes most often on Congressional matters, Armed Forces and National Security, and Economics and Public Finance. On Congressional procedure, she votes against more often than in favor. On Armed Forces bills, she votes in favor more often than against — she voted yes on the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act and voted against resolutions to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran. On Economics and Public Finance, she voted in favor of bills like the American Access to Banking Act and the Keeping Deposits Local Act.

E000071.narrative: Ellzey votes most often on congressional procedure, defense, and federal spending. On armed forces and national security bills, he votes in favor more often than against — he voted yes on the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act and no on a measure directing the removal of U.S. forces from Lebanon. On international affairs, he also votes in favor more often than against, though he voted against a bill authorizing support for Ukraine. His votes on government operations and politics are split evenly between in favor and against.

N000026.narrative: Nehls votes most often on congressional procedure, and on those votes he leans against the measures that come to the floor. On Armed Forces and National Security bills, he votes in favor more often than against, and he takes the same stance on Economics and Public Finance — voting yes on bills like the American Access to Banking Act and the Community Bank Deposit Access Act. On International Affairs, he votes in favor of most measures. He voted against resolutions that would have directed the President to remove U.S. forces from Lebanon and from hostilities with Iran, as well as against a bill to authorize support for Ukraine.

D000399.narrative: Doggett votes most often on congressional procedures, defense and national security, and economics and public finance. He votes in favor of most bills about congressional procedures and government operations. On economics and public finance, he votes against bills more often than in favor. On defense and national security, his votes are close to even — he voted yes on resolutions directing the removal of U.S. forces from Lebanon and Iran, but voted no on a military construction and Veterans Affairs appropriations bill. His votes on international affairs are also about evenly split.

K000401.narrative: Kiley votes in favor of most bills related to armed forces and national security issues and international affairs. He votes against most bills about energy policy, economics and public finance, and congressional procedures. He voted in favor of declaring Iran a sponsor of terrorism and blocking new energy efficiency rules for home appliances. He voted against stopping U.S. military action against Iran without congressional approval and against speeding up mining for metals on federal lands.
